doctrine: Strategic Autonomy & Multi-Alignment (Vishwa Mitra) — India positions itself as a 'Vishwa Mitra' (Global Friend) and leading voice of the Global South, refusing formal military alliances in favor of issue-based coalitions. New Delhi combines deep strategic and defense convergence with the United States in the Indo-Pacific while sustaining vital defense and energy ties with Russia.
strategic_priorities: Deter Chinese territorial revisionism along the Line of Actual Control and counter encirclement in the Indian Ocean ('String of Pearls')
Assert role as the primary 'Net Security Provider' in the Indian Ocean Region (IOR) and protect maritime trade chokepoints from Hormuz to Malacca
Deepen operational and defense industrial co-production with the United States and Quad partners (iCET, GE jet engine technology transfer, MQ-9B UAVs)
Preserve strategic defense legacy and discounted hydrocarbon access with Russia despite Western sanctions pressure
Promote Global South leadership, reform of multilateral institutions (permanent UN Security Council seat), and alternative payment arrangements
priority_regions: Indian Ocean Littoral & South Asia ('Neighborhood First' policy — Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Maldives, Nepal, Bhutan, Mauritius, Seychelles)
Indo-Pacific (Quad partners: USA, Japan, Australia; ASEAN maritime neighbors: Vietnam, Philippines, Indonesia)
Middle East / West Asia (I2U2 grouping, India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor [IMEC], UAE, Saudi Arabia, Israel)
Eurasia & Global South (Russia, Central Asian republics, African Union partnership)

cooperates_closely_with: United States (Major Defense Partner, Quad member, high-tech cooperation through iCET, bilateral military exercises [Malabar, Yudh Abhyas])
Russia ('Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership', major arms supplier, nuclear power collaborator at Kudankulam, discounted crude)
France (foremost European strategic partner, supplier of Rafale fighters, Scorpene submarines, joint space surveillance)
Japan & Australia (Quad anchors, reciprocal military logistics pacts, supply chain resilience initiatives)
Israel (close defense, counter-terrorism, agricultural technology, and surveillance systems partner)
United Arab Emirates & Saudi Arabia (crucial energy suppliers, trade partners, and destinations for 9M+ Indian diaspora)
competes_or_disputes_with: China (direct territorial disputes along the 3,488 km Himalayan border, competition for maritime dominance in the Indian Ocean, trade deficits)
Pakistan (historical rivalry over Jammu & Kashmir, cross-border terrorism concerns, opposition to CPEC transit through disputed territory)
cooperation_and_competition.notes: India's foreign policy has transitioned from defensive non-alignment to confident multi-alignment. New Delhi leverages its massive market, democratic credentials, and geographic position to maximize national interest across competing global blocs, maintaining that independent decision-making is an essential sovereign prerogative.

_meta.data_quality: sourced/analytical synthesis based on Ministry of External Affairs Annual Reports, National Security Council formulations, and speeches by Dr. S. Jaishankar
